title: Portable and sensitive approach for hydrazine detection via silver nanoparticles formation: A novel approach for chemical sensing
author: Khan, Zaibi, et al.

steps.title: Prepare silver ion solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve silver salt in ultrapure water to obtain a silver ion concentration of 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹ (the optimized condition; note that Figure 3 also lists 25 mmol L⁻¹), adjust the solution to pH 7.5, and add Brij‑35 as stabilizer (amount as used in the original study).

steps.title: Make hydrazine stock solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a hydrazine stock standard at 2.0 mmol L⁻¹ by adding the appropriate amount of hydrazine to ultrapure water.

steps.title: Prepare working hydrazine standards
steps.instruction: Dilute the 2.0 mmol L⁻¹ stock with ultrapure water to obtain working solutions covering the analytical range of 0.3 to 100 nmol L⁻¹ hydrazine.

steps.title: Filter environmental samples
steps.instruction: Pass each environmental aqueous sample through a 0.45 µm filter paper; the filtrate can be used directly for analysis.

steps.title: Initiate AgNP formation reaction
steps.instruction: In a reaction vessel, mix the silver ion solution (with Brij‑35, pH 7.5) with the hydrazine sample or standard; allow the reduction to proceed for exactly 4.0 min at ambient temperature.

steps.title: Measure absorbance of reaction mixture
steps.instruction: After the 4.0‑min reaction, withdraw an aliquot of the mixture, transfer it into a quartz cuvette, and record the absorbance spectrum, noting the localized surface plasmon resonance peak at 420 nm.

steps.title: Optional smartphone color analysis
steps.instruction: Capture a photo of the reacted solution and use a smartphone app to perform RGB color analysis for portable quantification of hydrazine (range 15.0–50.0 nmol L⁻¹).
